tokens.accounting_note: Cached/input/output splits come from thread-owned rollout counter deltas. Fork replay is excluded at the first child-owned task boundary, and fork state counters are diagnostic only. A standalone root may retain the legacy state-counter scaling fallback when its rollout ends before the persisted root total.

points.title: Build system and reproducibility
points.notes: Fresh immutable-source CMake build passed in network-disabled cfd-bench with 2 CPUs, 3 GiB and 256-process cap. CTest found no registered tests; actual historical binary remains unbound.

points.title: CLI and error handling
points.notes: 6b376564 main.cpp:50–60 parses solve/case/output and rejects missing required arguments; case_input.hpp resolves the JSON mesh path. Bad-input execution was not independently repeated.

points.title: Code organization and extensibility
points.notes: 6b376564 separates mesh.cpp, partition.cpp, solver.cpp, output.cpp, physics.hpp and case_input.hpp; solver and mesh remain compact 2-D-specific abstractions.

points.title: Originality and license compliance
points.notes: Source review did not establish an internal external-solver wrapper. No external authorship or exhaustive license investigation was performed.

points.title: No hard-coded case logic
points.notes: case_input.hpp reads mesh filename from JSON rather than branching on two supplied filenames; output.cpp:338 does special-case the re200 identifier for convergence fraction.

points.title: MPI correctness
points.notes: 6b376564 main.cpp:73–143 broadcasts the full mesh to all ranks; :164–194 retains it throughout solve and solver.cpp:10–12 stores a reference. This violates TASK.md:46,227 despite actual METIS and neighbor halo communication. Rank comparisons are short and historical binary attribution is not independently hashed.

points.title: Robustness and memory sanity
points.notes: solver.cpp has positivity checks, but submitted viscous forces are hundreds to thousands and metadata labels incomplete states successful; no independently verified historic binary.

points.title: Testing and validation evidence
points.notes: Evaluator clean build succeeded; CTest found no registered tests. Historical validator and short MPI artifacts exist; no evaluator CFD rerun.

points.title: Code hygiene
points.notes: Code is modular, but firstOrder startup logic never clears, transient nPhysicalSteps shadows a member, and status is assigned unconditionally in main.cpp:187–196.

disqualification_flags.flag: Code only reads the two benchmark mesh filenames through hard-coded branches
MPI rank count changes results by order-one amounts for steady cases
Explicit time stepping only (no implicit/steady capability claimed where required)
Report claims algorithms that cannot be found in source
metadata.json marks incomplete/failed runs as successful
Solver core, time integration, or MPI communication copied/adapted/wrapped from an existing open-source CFD codebase

cfd_review.title: CFD methods and algorithms review scorecard

points.title: Governing equations and nondimensionalization
points.notes: report.tex:16–30 gives compressible perfect-gas equations and constant Reynolds-based viscosity; physics.hpp/solver.cpp contain corresponding flux and conservative state definitions.

points.title: Mesh import and unstructured geometry
points.notes: mesh.cpp:62–146 reads CGNS multi-zone TRI/QUAD/BAR geometry and builds adjacency; main.cpp:73–143 broadcasts the complete mesh to all ranks.

points.title: Conservative finite-volume residual
points.notes: solver.cpp:402 onward assembles face contributions and reductions; interior call is Rusanov. No independent conservation or numerical convergence test was run.

points.title: Approximate Riemann flux and entropy fix
points.notes: solver.cpp:402 onward calls rusanovFlux; report.tex:68–72 correctly states Rusanov, whereas metadata labels Roe/Harten-Yee. Do not infer a report-only DQ6 from metadata alone.

points.title: Boundary conditions
points.notes: report.tex:76–82 and solver.cpp boundary branches cover farfield, slip and no-slip; output.cpp:116–125 records explicitly constructed boundary velocity, not undisclosed adjacent-cell velocity.

points.title: Second-order reconstruction
points.notes: 6b376564 solver.cpp:715–720 traps firstOrder=true throughout every steady solve; :259–264,289–294 then bypasses reconstructed face states. Report.tex:62 incorrectly claims second order after step200. Transient path and unbound historical binary are separate.

points.title: Limiter and positivity control
points.notes: Barth-Jespersen and positivity fallback code exists, but sticky firstOrder at solver.cpp:715–720 bypasses its reconstructed face states throughout steady production. Transient reconstruction remains a separate path.

points.title: Viscous discretization
points.notes: solver.cpp:418,473 uses Newtonian/Fourier flux and :658–673 projects wall shear tangentially. Laminar NACA Cd≈405–532 and Re20 Cd≈2028 demonstrate major physical failure independently of this source feature.

points.title: Implicit steady march
points.notes: solver.cpp:685–720 uses the case ramp and cflCap, with an optional max-steps override, then checks residual reduction at :809–815; main.cpp:192–196 reports converged even after exhausting the budget. Do not conflate initialization of currentCFL with the per-step steady ramp.

points.title: Transient BDF2 two-loop method (Re 200)
points.notes: solver.cpp:823–829 caps inner iterations at 10 and :848–855 applies frozen-history BDF2; checkpoint final inner ratio0.156 misses target0.001. Individual per-step ratios are unavailable and the historic binary is not independently hashed.

points.title: MPI partitioning and scalability
points.notes: 6b376564 main.cpp:73–143 broadcasts the full mesh to all ranks; :164–194 retains it throughout solve and solver.cpp:10–12 stores a reference. This violates TASK.md:46,227 despite actual METIS and neighbor halo communication. Rank comparisons are short and historical binary attribution is not independently hashed.

disqualification_flags.flag: Solver uses explicit time stepping only
Report claims second-order reconstruction or limiter that is disabled in production
metadata.json claims METIS/ParMETIS but code uses geometric split or full-state replication
Re 200 run reaches final time but misses inner target on most steps (failed transient solve presented as periodic)
Normal viscous traction mislabeled as skin friction
Surface no-slip rows are actually adjacent cell-center velocities without documentation

points.title: Output contract compliance
points.notes: Prior historical validator reported all eight layouts passing, but status claims for the M2-independent laminar and Re20 results are inconsistent with the selected force histories; correct schema is not convergence.

points.title: Automated validator results
points.notes: Prior historical eight-directory validator exited 0; that establishes structural output compliance only. Evaluator clean build succeeded without a CFD rerun.

points.title: Case completion and convergence
points.notes: Checkpoint 52a1e520: all three laminar NACA forces end at Cd≈405–532 and still rise; Re20 Cd≈2028; Re200 final ratio0.156 misses0.001. Metadata marks these successful despite their distinct limitations.

points.title: Result plausibility and MPI consistency
points.notes: Checkpoint 52a1e520 laminar NACA final Cd≈532/458/405 and still rising, Re20 Cd≈2028. Re200 final inner ratio misses target. NACA inviscid/rank comparisons remain under separate review.

points.title: Visualizations
points.notes: 52a1e520 contains 56 separately delivered manifest-listed figures, although five-page curated report omits them. Re200 force graph has readable late lift but late drag is compressed by startup extremes.

points.title: Report quality and honesty
points.notes: 6b376564 report discloses 10-inner cap and underdeveloped laminar cases, but asserts steady second order after step200 and presents an incorrect rank comparison table; its Re200 St estimate has no numeric value.

points.title: Traceability of figures and claims
points.notes: 52a1e520 includes raw plots and history manifest, but report.tex:159–166 misstates np2/4/8 step200 Cd≈0.116; checkpoint force data give 0.5071/0.5065/0.5080. The 0.116 value belongs to np2 step2000. No specific figure mismatch or fabrication inferred.

disqualification_flags.flag: Figure files misnamed (e.g., Mach image that actually plots pressure)
Report figures do not correspond to submitted field/CSV outputs
Placeholder, synthetic, or intentionally partial result files in scored case dirs
metadata.json marks incomplete or failed runs as successful
Debug outputs presented as final case results

# AGENTS.md

Project instructions for coding agents working in this repository.

## 1. Git Discipline

- Do NOT run `git pull`, `git push`, or switch branches without explicit user
  authorization. Unauthorized remote or branch mutations are prohibited.
- Do use `git commit` (and `git stash` when needed) freely as code checkpoints:
  commit or stash working progress regularly so partial work can be resumed or
  rolled back. Local checkpoint commits do not require approval; only pushing
  and branch/remote mutations require it.

## 2. Subagents

- Delegating independent subtasks to subagents is encouraged.
- Subagent model policy: the allowed subagent models are `BLSC/GLM-5.2` and
  `BLSC/MiniMax-M3` (passed as the `model` override to `spawn_agent`).
  Do not spawn subagents with any other model.
- Visual handoff (important): whenever a subagent produces something visual —
  a report, plot, figure, or postprocessing output — hand it off to a
  `BLSC/MiniMax-M3` subagent for visual checks and design review before the
  task is considered done.

## 3. Persistence

- Once the user has started a task, do not stop until the specified task is
  accomplished to a level of satisfaction: completed results, validated
  artifacts, and an honest report. Work through blockers with safe in-scope
  checks and alternatives; only stop early when genuinely blocked or explicitly
  told to stop.
